Challenge: benchmark:sql-injection-golden
Current phase: INTAKE

Candidate vulnerability categories: SQLI

Description: SQL_INJECTION benchmark case for sql-injection-golden.

payload.goal: Fetch GET / and GET /health and dump the FULL response (status, headers, complete body). Parse the HTML for forms, input names, links, hidden fields, inline scripts, and script src references. Identify the real application surface and any parameters that reach a backend query.
payload.rationale: Only '/' and '/health' return 200; the body of '/' is the untapped gold that reveals the actual injection point.

payload.goal: Enumerate and fetch static/JS assets referenced by '/', grep the JS for endpoint paths, query strings, parameter names, and fetch/axios/XHR call shapes to recover the true SQL-injection route and parameter that blind path guessing missed.
payload.rationale: SPA/benchmark apps expose their real API routes and parameter names in client-side JS, not in guessed paths.

payload.goal: On the confirmed live endpoints ('/' and '/health'), fuzz query parameters (common names: id, q, search, name, user, page, item, product, cat, filter) with error-based probes (single quote, double quote, backslash, numeric expression) and compare baseline vs injected responses (status, length, body diff, error text). Record any parameter whose response changes only when the SQL syntax is altered, and repeat to confirm stability.
payload.rationale: Establishes whether a parameter on the live pages reaches a SQL query via the error channel before escalating to boolean/time.

payload.goal: GET / and GET /health; persist the COMPLETE raw response (status, all headers incl. Server/X-Powered-By/Set-Cookie/Content-Type, and full body text) as verified facts, then extract every <form>, input[name], anchor href, inline <script>, and any reflected query value from the body. This establishes the ground-truth injection surface.
payload.rationale: The graph has no verified body for either live endpoint, so all SQLi work is blind. The prior content-discovery intent was marked route_exhausted without producing a body fact, so this direction must be genuinely completed before anything else is reliable.

payload.goal: Probe the non-query injection surface: send POST/PUT requests to '/' and '/health' with JSON and form bodies using plausible field names (id, q, search, name, username, product, item), plus try alternate methods (POST/OPTIONS/HEAD), looking for behavior/error/timing differences that indicate a body-path SQL query. New direction: the open intents only cover GET query-parameter fuzzing.
payload.rationale: Given only '/' and /health are live (FastAPI-style surface with 404 openapi), the injectable sink may be a POST/JSON body param rather than a GET query param. This is a distinct surface from the in-flight query-param fuzzing.

payload.goal: Fingerprint the backend to choose the correct SQL dialect: record response headers/framework signatures and compare baseline vs a single-quote/malformed probe on each live endpoint's discovered parameter, classifying whether errors are reflected, boolean-different, or time-delayed (SQLite vs MySQL vs Postgres).
payload.rationale: Knowing the framework/DBMS (uvicorn+SQLite vs Flask+MySQL) determines payload syntax and which channel (error/boolean/time) is viable, preventing wasted cycles resending the wrong payload family.

payload.goal: Detect routes that exist but reject GET: for the candidate names already implied by the app's guesses (/warranty, /verify, /check, /query, /lookup, /track, /search, plus /products, /items, /users, /customer, /record, /api/lookup, /api/search) send POST and PUT with both form-encoded and JSON scalar bodies (e.g. id=1, inquiry=1, code=1) and record status codes — treat 405/400/415/500 as endpoint-exists signals distinct from 404, and immediately follow any non-404 with a single-quote variant to see whether the body/status changes.
payload.rationale: All discovery so far has been GET-only, so a POST-only injection endpoint would look identical to a nonexistent path. The 404 wall on /search, /lookup, /track is only proven for GET; method-based existence detection is a genuinely different question from the open GET-parameter fuzzing intent.

payload.goal: Force a server-side exception/traceback on the two live endpoints ('/' and '/health'): send type-confusion and boundary inputs — repeated params (?a=1&a=2), array syntax (?a[]=1), out-of-range integers, non-UTF-8/percent-encoded bytes, %00, extremely long values — and also probe /console and the Werkzeug debugger surface (__debugger__). Persist any 500 response body verbatim; a Flask traceback would reveal the source path, the SQL string, and the real parameter name.
payload.rationale: Error-based SQL probing only works if DB errors propagate; an application-level traceback is an independent channel that works even when SQL errors are swallowed, and would collapse the whole parameter-guessing problem.

payload.goal: Targeted source/config/artifact exposure check (not link-following): request benchmark-typical non-HTML files — /flag, /flag.txt, /app.py, /main.py, /server.py, /requirements.txt, /db.sqlite3, /data.db, /.git/HEAD, /Dockerfile, /source, /debug, /api/flag — and record exact status plus body of anything that is not 404.
payload.rationale: Every probe so far assumed HTML/JS assets. The dead-end note that no static assets exist was derived only from guessed JS/CSS paths, so source/DB/flag artifacts on a server-rendered app remain untested and would give the schema or the flag directly.

payload.goal: Establish a boolean-blind injection channel on the two live endpoints ('/' and '/health'): record a byte-stable baseline (body length + hash), then for each candidate parameter (id, q, search, name, user, item, product, cat, page) send a TRUE predicate and a FALSE predicate (e.g. `' AND 1=1-- -` vs `' AND 1=2-- -` and numeric `1 AND 1=1` vs `1 AND 1=2`) at least 3x each, and report any parameter/channel where the response length/hash/status flips consistently with the predicate truth value.

payload.goal: Reflection / catch-all detection on '/': confirm whether the app echoes or routes arbitrary user input — test GET /<random-token>, GET / with a unique random query param (?<rand>=<rand>), and a random header/cookie value, then grep each response body and Location/Set-Cookie headers for the injected token. Report every place a supplied string is reflected verbatim (that reflected element is the real injection point).
payload.rationale: Parameter name alone has never been confirmed; reflection detection turns guesswork into evidence by finding which input reaches the response/query on the live '/' page [#1].

payload.goal: Arbitration: reconcile the two overlapping capture intents, cancel/close the six verifier intents on trivial 404 facts (they confirm nothing useful), and declare which single request element (query param / POST field / reflected path / header) is the canonical injection channel based on I1/I2 results — then direct the next data-extraction step (UNION or blind character extraction to recover the flag).
payload.rationale: Graph shows duplicate capture directions and six verify intents for irrelevant 404s, plus conflicting 'route_exhausted' vs open re-proposals — this is a route loop that needs arbitration before more intents are spent.

payload.goal: Replace hand-guessed path names with real wordlist discovery: run ffuf/gobuster/feroxbuster against the target root with a standard directory wordlist plus extension set (.php,.py,.txt,.json,.bak,.sql,.db,.html) and status/length filtering, then auto-fetch every non-404 hit with full body capture and grep it for forms, input names, parameter names, JS fetch/XHR calls and flag strings. Wordlist brute force plus extension fuzzing is a genuinely different, higher-coverage discovery method than the exhausted guess lists, and it feeds contexts the parameter fuzzers cannot find on their own.

payload.goal: Open a TIME-based channel on '/' and '/health' with repeated measurement: for a compact sweep of plausible parameter names (id, q, s, search, name, user, product, item, page, cat, filter, track, lookup, warranty) send baseline vs SLEEP/pg_sleep/heavy-subquery payloads in quoted and numeric boundaries, 3 repeats each, and compare median response time while requiring body/status stability. payload.rationale: Error-based was declared exhausted on status codes alone and boolean-blind is noisy/unspecified; the timing channel was never attempted. It is the standard fallback when errors are suppressed and bodies are static, and it is measurable without a visible output marker.

payload.goal: Attack the request-body and verb surface that has never been touched: on the two live endpoints '/' [#1] and '/health' [#5], first enumerate allowed methods (OPTIONS, and probe HEAD/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/TRACE to see which return something other than 404/405), then send SQL-breaking payloads inside POST form bodies and JSON bodies (keys id, q, search, name, user, page, item, product, cat, filter, table, db) and compare status, body and content-length against a benign body of identical shape. Record raw requests/responses.
payload.rationale: Every existing SQLi intent targets the query string, headers or cookies; nothing in the graph tests POST/JSON bodies or verb tampering. If '/' is a form handler, that is the only channel that can be injectable — and per the channel-escalation prior, the boundary differs per channel, so a payload that failed in the query string can succeed in a body.

payload.goal: Replace the useless bare-directory guessing with combinatorial endpoint+parameter probing: run ffuf (or equivalent) with a short application-shaped endpoint wordlist (item, items, product, products, user, users, news, post, article, cat, category, list, detail, view, order, record, lookup, search, query) crossed with parameter templates (?id=1, ?id=1', ?id=1", /1, /1', ?q=, ?name=), and keep only responses whose status/content-length differs from the plain 404 baseline; for any hit, immediately run a 3x repeated true/false predicate differential to decide whether an injection point exists.
payload.rationale: The only route discovery done so far was ~40 hand-picked wordlist entries without parameters, which cannot find a route that is defined as '/<resource>?id=N'. Real SQLi benchmarks are almost always of that shape; the dead-end claim that this is a 'minimal server-rendered Flask app' came from those same no-parameter guesses and is not proven.

payload.goal: Use a shell/raw-HTTP client (curl -sS -i, NOT the metadata-only http_request tool) to fetch GET / and GET /health and persist the COMPLETE response verbatim — status line, all headers (Server, X-Powered-By, Set-Cookie), and the full HTML body. From the body, enumerate every form action, input/parameter name, link, inline script, and query-string candidate, and pin those as facts. If / returns a form, immediately submit it with a normal value to learn the observable (length/marker) before touching payloads.

All downstream 'no parameter found / route_exhausted' conclusions rest on this tooling gap, so raw body capture is the single highest-value unblocker and must be done with a client that returns actual text.

payload.goal: Probe the Flask app for source/config/debug disclosure on the confirmed live host: GET /console (Werkzeug interactive debugger -> potential RCE), /app.py, /main.py, /server.py, /wsgi.py, /requirements.txt, /.env, /config.py, /Dockerfile, /.git/config, /proc/self/environ.
